content: Thymol is a monoterpene phenol derived from cymene, with the chemical formula C10H13OH. It is isomeric with carvacrol and is naturally found in thyme oil. Thymol can be extracted as a white crystalline substance that has a pleasant aromatic odor and exhibits strong antiseptic properties. It is also referred to as hydroxy cymene. Thymol has demonstrated efficacy in controlling varroa mites, which are parasitic mites affecting bee colonies. Additionally, it has a minor application in book restoration; books with mold damage can be sealed in bags with thymol crystals to eliminate fungal spores before rebinding. Thymol is also utilized as a preservative in halothane, an inhalational anesthetic agent. In a 1994 report published by five major cigarette manufacturers, thymol was identified as one of the 599 additives used in cigarettes. Its inclusion serves the purpose of enhancing flavor.
